must_have.required_content: Correct Start2 entity performing the service, matched to client jurisdiction, real registered address.
must_have.rationale: Wrong entity means wrong tax treatment, wrong court, wrong company on the hook.

draft.language:
This Agreement is made between [Start2 Entity Legal Name] ("Start2"), a company with its registered address at [Registered Address], and 

[Company Full Name] ("Company"), a company with its registered address at [Company Address]. 

Start2 and Company are hereinafter individually referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".

must_have.required_content: Short statement of what the client is and what Start2 is delivering, no marketing copy beyond standard boilerplate.
must_have.rationale: Recitals get pulled into scope disputes when operative clauses are vague.

draft.language:
WHEREAS:
A. Start2 and Company wish to enter into this service agreement ("Agreement") to set out the terms on which Start2 will provide the Service (as defined below) to Company.
B. Start2 is a global innovation platform that helps growth-oriented startups, corporations, investors, and governments shape and scale ventures with growth potential.
C. Company is [Company Description].
D. Start2 will provide [Service Description] to Company (the "Service").
draft.notes: C and D must be completed for every deal before the draft goes to the client. Never leave as a placeholder.

must_have.required_content: What Start2 does, what it does not do, deliverables list, exclusions.
must_have.rationale: Without a completed appendix, scope is whatever the client later says it was.

draft.language:
3.1 The contents of the Service to be delivered by Start2 under this Agreement are set out in Appendix 1 (the "Scope"), which the Parties shall agree and attach before execution of this Agreement.
3.2 Appendix 1 shall specify, at minimum: the deliverables Start2 will provide, any exclusions, and the number of participants or startups covered (if applicable).
draft.notes: Appendix 1 must be a completed, deal-specific scope before signature, never left blank and never carried over unedited from a different client's deal.

must_have.required_content: Fixed start and end date, mechanism for what happens if the program cannot start on time.
must_have.rationale: Fixes the window Start2 is obliged to deliver in.

draft.language:
4.1 This Agreement shall run from [Start Date] to [End Date] (the "Term"), subject to any extension mutually agreed by the Parties in writing.
4.2 Start2 shall complete the Service within the Term, subject to Clause [Force Majeure].

must_have.required_content: Fee amount, currency, tax treatment, plain-language trigger for each payment tranche.
must_have.rationale: This is the clause most exposed to ambiguity in the current templates.

draft.language:
5.1 Company shall pay Start2 a Service Fee of [Currency] [Amount], excluding [applicable tax/GST/VAT] (the "Service Fee"), for the Service.
5.2 The Service Fee shall be paid as follows: [payment schedule per Decision D-01 — e.g. 100% upfront per phase, invoiced 7 days before each phase, due within 7 days of invoice] OR [50% on signing, non-refundable on Commencement; 50% on Completion]. "Commencement" means [defined event, completed per deal]. "Completion" means [defined event, completed per deal].
5.3 Payment shall be made in [Currency].
5.4 The Service Fee shall be paid without deduction or withholding for any tax, duty, or charge. Where such deduction or withholding is required by law, Company shall gross up the payment so that Start2 receives the full Service Fee net of such deduction.
5.5 Payment shall be made to Start2's bank account: [Bank Details].
draft.notes: Payment schedule (5.2) depends on Decision D-01, not yet settled. Never leave Commencement/Completion as an open placeholder in a signed agreement, this is the #1 defect found in the current templates.
placeholders: [50% on signing, non-refundable on Commencement; 50% on Completion]
[payment schedule per Decision D-01 — e.g. 100% upfront per phase, invoiced 7 days before each phase, due within 7 days of invoice]

must_have.required_content: Client may not withhold or deduct any amount from the Service Fee against an alleged claim, counterclaim, or dispute, whether or not related to this agreement.
must_have.rationale: Without this, a client with a service complaint can unilaterally withhold payment rather than raise the dispute through the agreed process, effectively self-authorising a discount.
must_have.mutuality: One-sided in practice, this protects Start2's cash position specifically

draft.language: Company shall not withhold, deduct, or set off any amount from the Service Fee against any alleged claim, counterclaim, or dispute, whether or not related to this Agreement, except as otherwise expressly agreed by Start2 in writing.

must_have.clause: Late payment: interest and right to suspend
must_have.required_content: A stated interest rate on any amount overdue, and an express right for Start2 to suspend delivery of the Service on written notice if payment is overdue by a stated number of days.
must_have.rationale: Currently, simple late payment (short of insolvency) only reaches the general "material breach, 14-day cure" catch-all. No interest applies, and Start2 has no clean right to pause delivery while chasing an overdue invoice without being accused of breaching the agreement itself.
must_have.mutuality: One-sided, this is a remedy that only makes sense running from client to Start2

draft.language:
7.1 Any amount not paid by its due date shall accrue interest at [X]% per annum (or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, if lower), calculated daily from the due date until paid.
7.2 If any payment is overdue by more than [X] days, Start2 may suspend delivery of the Service on written notice to Company, without this being treated as a breach by Start2, until payment is received in full.
draft.notes: Interest rate and suspension trigger (days) are open figures, not yet set.

must_have.required_content: What each side must not disclose, standard carve-outs, survives termination.
must_have.rationale: Protects Start2 methodology and client business information equally.
must_have.mutuality: Mutual, except the carve-out letting Start2's startups share information with potential clients, experts, and mentors, which is one-directional in substance, functionally necessary for the program to work, not a concession.

must_have.required_content: Neither party may assign, delegate, novate, or subcontract the agreement as a whole, or a material part of it, to a third party without the other's prior written consent. Carve-out: Start2 may engage mentors, experts, consultants, and other personnel to carry out the Service in the ordinary course of delivering the program, without this being treated as an assignment or subcontracting requiring the Company's consent, provided Start2 remains responsible for their performance.
must_have.rationale: Start2's delivery model depends on engaging external mentors and experts for every program. Without the carve-out, a literal reading of the assignment restriction treats every mentor engagement as unauthorised subcontracting, a technical breach on nearly every deal, and gives the client an argument to dispute delivery. Start2 remaining responsible for engaged personnel's performance keeps this consistent with the Warranties clause and the general Indemnity clause.
must_have.mutuality: Mutual on the restriction itself, one-sided on the carve-out (only Start2 engages third parties to deliver the Service)

draft.language:
9.1 Neither Party shall assign, novate, delegate, or subcontract this Agreement, or a material part of it, to a third party without the other Party's prior written consent.
9.2 For the avoidance of doubt, Start2 may engage mentors, experts, consultants, and other personnel to carry out the Service in the ordinary course of delivering the program, and this shall not be treated as an assignment or subcontracting requiring Company's consent under Clause 9.1, provided Start2 remains responsible for their performance under this Agreement.

must_have.clause: Independent contractor / no agency or partnership
must_have.required_content: States that nothing in the agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency, or employment relationship between the parties, and neither party has authority to bind the other.
must_have.rationale: Start2 sits between a corporate client and third-party startups it introduces in matching and delegation programs. Without this clause, a client or a startup could argue Start2 acted as the client's agent, exposing Start2 to liability for decisions it did not make.

draft.language: Nothing in this Agreement constitutes either Party as the agent, employee, partner, or representative of the other. Neither Party has authority to bind, represent, or assume any obligation on behalf of the other without that Party's prior written consent.

must_have.required_content: How formal notice (breach, termination, proposed amendment) must be given: in writing, to a named address, attention person, and email per party, with a deemed-receipt rule stated separately for each delivery method (personal delivery, registered mail domestic vs. international, fax, email).
must_have.rationale: Amendment and Termination both already require "written notice." Without this clause, nothing says what counts as written notice, where it must be sent, or when it is deemed received, so a client can dispute that notice was ever validly given. The per-method deemed-receipt structure (under Refence column) removes ambiguity about exactly when a notice takes effect.

must_have.required_content: Agreement may only be revised or amended by a written amendment signed by both parties after mutual discussion. No change by conduct, email, or verbal agreement.
must_have.rationale: Stops a client claiming a scope or fee change was agreed by email or in a call with a program manager. Forces every change through the same review path as the original signature.

draft.language: This Agreement may only be amended by a written instrument signed by both Parties. No amendment by conduct, email exchange, or verbal agreement shall be effective.

must_have.required_content: Defined default events, written notice and cure mechanism, payment preserved for work done to date of termination.
must_have.rationale: Without the "paid for work done to date" line, early termination could be argued to release the client from paying for delivered work.

must_have.clause: No cost committed before payment received
must_have.required_content: Internal control, referenced in the payment clause commentary, not a client-facing clause.
must_have.rationale: Cash exposure control.

must_have.required_content: Any cost Start2 has committed, incurred, or paid to a third party (mentors, venue, travel, logistics, subcontractors) in connection with delivering the program, before the date of cancellation or termination, is for the Company's account and is due and payable to Start2. This applies regardless of which party caused the cancellation or the reason for it, including force majeure. This is separate from, and in addition to, settlement of the Service Fee for work performed to date.
must_have.rationale: Start2 fronts real third-party cash costs to run these programs once a tranche is received. A cancelled venue booking or a committed mentor fee is rarely refundable to Start2 in full. Without this clause, Start2 can be left holding costs it can no longer recover from the third party, while the client argues those costs should come out of Start2's own pocket rather than being reimbursed. This is the other half of the no-cost-before-payment rule: that internal rule stops Start2 committing unfunded cost in the first place, this clause stops the client clawing back cost Start2 already funded and spent properly once a tranche is received.
must_have.mutuality: One-sided. This is Start2 recovering its own committed costs, the client does not commit equivalent third-party costs.
must_have.cap_position: No cap, this is a cost-reimbursement mechanism, not a liability cap, it should equal the actual cost incurred

draft.language: Where this Agreement is cancelled or terminated for any reason, including under Clause [Force Majeure], any cost that Start2 has committed, incurred, or paid to a third party (including mentors, venue, travel, logistics, or sub-contractors) in connection with delivering the Service before the date of cancellation is for Company's account and is due and payable to Start2. This is in addition to, and not in substitution for, Start2's entitlement to the Service Fee for work performed to date under Clause [Termination for Cause].

must_have.required_content: Start2 warrants it will perform the Service with reasonable skill and care using suitably qualified personnel. Company warrants that information and materials it supplies are accurate and that its signatory has authority to bind it.
must_have.rationale: Sets the performance standard as reasonable skill and care rather than a guaranteed outcome, and puts responsibility for inaccurate client-supplied information back on the client, not on Start2.
must_have.cap_position: Breach of warranty falls under the general liability cap unless separately carved out

draft.language:
15.1 Start2 warrants that it will perform the Service with reasonable skill and care, using personnel with suitable qualifications and experience.
15.2 Company warrants that: (a) all information and materials it provides to Start2 in connection with the Service are accurate and complete; and (b) its signatory to this Agreement has authority to bind Company.

must_have.required_content: Each party indemnifies the other for actual loss or damage caused by its breach or negligence, subject to the liability cap. This is the obligation to make good, distinct from the cap that limits how much.
must_have.rationale: Ensures the client bears responsibility for third-party claims caused by the client's own conduct, for example an IP dispute or injury arising from the client's own startups or staff during a program.
must_have.cap_position: Capped at total Service Fee, same pool as Limitation of Liability

draft.language:
16.1 Each Party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall indemnify and hold harmless the other Party, its affiliates, sub-contractors, licensors, licensees, and each of their respective officers, directors, agents, consultants, and employees (collectively, the "Indemnified Parties") from and against any and all loss, damage, expense (including legal costs on a solicitor and client basis), and liability (whether criminal or civil), except any indirect, special, or consequential loss or damage, suffered or incurred by the Indemnified Parties arising out of or in connection with the Indemnifying Party's breach of this Agreement, negligence, or wilful default, or that of its sub-contractors, licensees, or their respective officers, directors, agents, consultants, or employees.
16.2 Company shall indemnify Start2 against any third-party claim arising from the conduct, intellectual property, or materials of any startup or participant that Company puts forward for the Service.
16.3 The indemnity in this Clause is subject to the cap set out in Clause [Limitation of Liability], except for claims arising from a Party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
draft.notes: 16.2 closes a gap not present in the current templates: no client indemnity currently exists for claims caused by the client's own startups.

must_have.required_content: Exclusion of indirect/consequential loss, cap on direct loss tied to a defined measure.
must_have.rationale: Caps Start2's total exposure to a known number before signature.
must_have.cap_position: Total fees paid or payable, named carve-outs

draft.language:
17.1 Neither Party is liable to the other for indirect, special, or consequential loss, including loss of profits, revenue, or business opportunity, arising from this Agreement.

17.2 Except as set out in Clause 17.3, each Party's total liability to the other under this Agreement, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, is capped at the total Service Fee paid or payable under this Agreement.

17.3 For claims arising from breach of Clause [Confidentiality], Clause [Data Protection], or Clause [Intellectual Property], each Party's total liability to the other is capped instead at [a multiple, see Decision D-02] times the total Service Fee paid or payable under this Agreement.

17.4 Neither cap in Clause 17.2 or 17.3 applies to loss arising from a Party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
draft.notes: The higher multiple for confidentiality/data/IP breaches (Decision D-02) is not yet settled.

must_have.required_content: Standard carve-out excusing non-performance caused by events outside a party's control, with an explicit line excluding inability to meet financial obligations from qualifying as a force majeure event. Includes a long-stop: if the event continues beyond a stated period, the parties first discuss in good faith, for a capped window, whether to postpone or reschedule instead. If no agreement is reached within that window, either party may terminate on written notice, without liability beyond amounts already due under Cost Recovery on Cancellation.
must_have.rationale: Relieves Start2 of liability for delay from events like export-control suspensions or travel restriction. The explicit financial-obligations exclusion (under Refence column) stops a client ever arguing that a cash-flow problem is itself a force majeure event excusing non-payment.
must_have.reference_clause: If the ability of either party to perform any of its obligations under this Agreement is limited, delayed or prevented in whole or in part by reason of any cause or event beyond the reasonable control of such party, including but without limitation fire, storm, tempest, explosion, accident, breakdown of plant or machinery, strike and/or industrial dispute, war, civil strike or commotion, act of foreign enemy, epidemic, quarantine, health risk, terrorist activity, events of national emergency, hostilities (whether war be declared or not), law or act of or authorised by a government but excluding the inability to meet financial obligations (a "Force Majeure Event"), such party shall be excused, discharged or released without penalty or liability from its obligations under this Agreement to the extent and for the period that such performance is so limited, delayed or prevented PROVIDED that such party shall take all steps reasonably possible to mitigate the losses or damages caused by its failure or delay to perform its obligations under this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Force Majeure Event exceeds sixty (60) days in duration, either party shall have the right at any time thereafter during the continuance of such failure or delay, to terminate this Agreement by giving written notice to the other party.

draft.language:
18.1 If the ability of either party to perform any of its obligations under this Agreement is limited, delayed or prevented in whole or in part by reason of any cause or event beyond the reasonable control of such party, including but without limitation fire, storm, tempest, explosion, accident, breakdown of plant or machinery, strike and/or industrial dispute, war, civil strike or commotion, act of foreign enemy, epidemic, quarantine, health risk, terrorist activity, events of national emergency, hostilities (whether war be declared or not), law or act of or authorised by a government but excluding the inability to meet financial obligations (a "Force Majeure Event"), such party shall be excused, discharged or released without penalty or liability from its obligations under this Agreement to the extent and for the period that such performance is so limited, delayed or prevented provided that such party shall take all steps reasonably possible to mitigate the losses or damages caused by its failure or delay to perform its obligations under this Agreement. 
18.2 If a Force Majeure Event under Clause [Force Majeure] continues for more than sixty (60) days, the Parties shall first discuss in good faith, for up to [14] days, whether to postpone or reschedule the Service instead of terminating this Agreement.
18.3 If the Parties do not agree to postpone or reschedule within that period, either Party may terminate this Agreement on written notice to the other, without liability, other than for amounts already due under Clause [Cost Recovery on Cancellation].

must_have.required_content: Each party warrants it is not, and is not owned or controlled by, a sanctioned person or entity. Either party may suspend or terminate without the standard cure period if performance becomes restricted by export control, sanctions, or other government action, or if the other party becomes a sanctioned entity.
must_have.rationale: Start2 delivers cross-border programs to government-linked bodies (Ulsan Technopark, KIDP) across jurisdictions with active and changing export control regimes. Without this clause, Start2 has no clean exit if a government action makes continued performance illegal or commercially unsafe, and would have to rely on the general force majeure clause, which is not written with sanctions or export control in mind.

draft.language:
19.1 Each Party warrants that it is not, and is not owned or controlled by, a person or entity subject to sanctions under applicable law.
19.2 Either Party may suspend or terminate this Agreement on written notice, without the cure period in Clause [Termination for Cause], if performance becomes restricted by export control, sanctions, or other government action, or if the other Party becomes subject to sanctions.

must_have.required_content: Each party's pre-existing IP stays with that party. Start2 retains ownership of its own methodology, curriculum, frameworks and materials absolutely, licensed for use during the program only. Limited licence to use each other's name and logo, no transfer of ownership. A closing catch-all stating no rights other than those expressly set out in the clause are granted.
must_have.rationale: Start2's core asset is its methodology. Must not be assignable to the client through vague "developed by each other" language that does not distinguish pre-existing IP from program deliverables. The closing catch-all (under Refence column) removes any argument that a right was granted by implication.
must_have.mutuality: Mutual for each party's own creations. Asymmetric in that Start2's core methodology is never transferred, regardless of who commissioned the work.
must_have.cap_position: Infringement liability capped at the higher multiple, see Caps sheet
must_have.reference_clause: For the avoidance of doubt, no rights other than those set out in this clause 20 are granted. Save as provided in this clause, neither party shall use the other party’s intellectual property without the prior approval of the other party.

draft.language:
20.1 Start2 retains sole and exclusive ownership of all intellectual property rights, whether registered or not, in its pre-existing and independently developed materials, including its methodology, curriculum, frameworks, training materials, evaluation tools, software, platforms, databases, trademarks, trade names, logos, business plans, know-how, and processes, and any improvement, enhancement, or derivative work of the foregoing, however and whenever created, including during the course of delivering the Service. None of the foregoing is assigned or transferred to Company under this Agreement.
20.2 Company retains ownership of its own pre-existing intellectual property and confidential business information.
20.3 Program-specific deliverables prepared for Company's own cohort (such as mentor evaluation reports, session schedules, or feedback scores) are licensed to Company for its own internal use. This licence does not extend to the underlying methodology, tools, or materials used to produce them, which remain Start2's under Clause 20.1.
20.4 Each Party grants the other a limited, non-exclusive licence to use its name and logo for purposes connected with this Agreement, with no transfer of ownership.
20.5 For the avoidance of doubt, no rights other than those expressly set out in this Clause are granted.

must_have.required_content: Short clause on handling personal data of participants, mentors, client staff, referencing applicable law (PDPA Singapore, PIPA Korea, APPI Japan, PIPL China).
must_have.rationale: Start2 routinely processes participant and mentor personal data across four jurisdictions with active data protection regimes.

draft.language: Each Party shall comply with applicable data protection law in respect of any personal data processed in connection with this Agreement, including [PDPA (Singapore) / PIPA (Korea) / APPI (Japan) / PIPL (China), as applicable to the contracting entity], and shall only use such data for purposes connected with the Service.
draft.notes: Bracket the correct law per contracting entity when drafting the country-specific version.
placeholders: [PDPA (Singapore) / PIPA (Korea) / APPI (Japan) / PIPL (China), as applicable to the contracting entity]

must_have.required_content: For bilingual agreements (China, Korea), a clause stating which language version prevails in the event the two texts disagree.
must_have.rationale: The Execution Check already flags that bilingual versions must be checked against each other before signature. Without a precedence clause, a genuine translation discrepancy discovered after signature has no answer, both versions are equally binding, and a court or arbitrator has to guess at intent.

draft.language: This Agreement is executed in English [and Chinese / and Korean]. In the event of any discrepancy between the language versions, the English version shall prevail.
draft.notes: Only needed for bilingual agreements (China, Korea). Confirm English-prevails is the intended position before finalising, some government counterparties may push for the local-language version to prevail instead.

must_have.required_content: Law of the contracting entity's jurisdiction, arbitration seat matched to it, single arbitrator, English language.
must_have.rationale: Keeps disputes in a forum Start2's counsel can operate in, out of the client's home court by default.

draft.language:
23.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of [Singapore / Republic of Korea / Japan / People's Republic of China, per contracting entity].
23.2 In case of dispute between the parties arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity or termination, Parties shall in good faith endeavor to amicably resolve such dispute.
23.3 Failing which, such dispute shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration administered by the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (“SIAC”) in accordance with the Arbitration Rules of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (“SIAC Rules”) for the time being in force, which rules are deemed to be incorporated by reference in this Clause. The Tribunal shall consist of a single arbitrator to be appointed by the Chairman of the SIAC. The seat of the arbitration shall be in Singapore. The language of the arbitration shall be in English. The award of the arbitrator shall be final and binding upon the Parties. The costs and expenses of arbitration, including the compensation and expenses of the Arbitrator, shall be borne by the Parties as the Arbitrator may determine.
draft.notes: Already correct per entity in the current templates, carried forward.
placeholders: [Singapore / Republic of Korea / Japan / People's Republic of China, per contracting entity]

must_have.required_content: This agreement and its appendices are the entire agreement between the parties on this subject, superseding all prior discussions, drafts, side emails and verbal representations not incorporated into it. Includes a non-reliance line: neither party has a remedy for any statement made to it that it relied on in entering the agreement, unless that statement is written into the agreement itself.
must_have.rationale: Without it, a client can point to pre-signature emails, decks, or verbal assurances from a sales conversation as additional terms. This is what makes the Amendment clause (already Must Have) actually hold: change only happens in writing, signed by both, because nothing else counts as part of the deal. The non-reliance line (under Refence column) goes further, it also blocks a claim that the client relied on something a Start2 salesperson said outside the written document.
must_have.reference_clause:
This Agreement and its Schedules constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, proposals, representations, and discussions between the parties, whether verbal or written. There are no
understandings, agreements, representations, or warranties, expressed or implied, not expressly specified in this Agreement. Neither party shall have any remedy in respect of any statement made to it upon which it relied in entering into this Agreement.

draft.language: This Agreement and its Appendices constitute the entire agreement between the Parties on this subject and supersede all prior discussions, proposals, and representations, whether written or verbal. Neither Party has a remedy for any statement it relied on in entering this Agreement unless that statement is set out in this Agreement.
draft.notes: Non-reliance sentence adapted from the Enterprise Singapore exhibition agreement, Clause 15.1.

must_have.required_content: Express list of which clauses survive termination or expiry of the agreement: Confidentiality, Indemnity, Limitation of Liability, Dispute Resolution, and Data Protection.
must_have.rationale: Confidentiality already has its own explicit survival line. The other four do not. Without an express survival clause, a party could argue the liability cap or the arbitration requirement lapses the moment the contract ends, even for a claim about conduct that happened during the term.

draft.language: Clauses [Confidentiality], [Indemnity], [Limitation of Liability], [Governing Law and Dispute Resolution], and [Data Protection] survive termination or expiry of this Agreement.

must_have.required_content: Each party may execute by electronic signature (e.g. Zoho Sign), each counterpart is deemed an original, and all counterparts together form one instrument.
must_have.rationale: Actual practice already uses electronic signature, the KIDP China agreement was executed on Zoho Sign, but every template still reads "the parties prepare and sign 2 copies...and keep 1 copy respectively," wet-ink language that does not describe how Start2 actually signs.

draft.language: This Agreement may be executed electronically, including by way of Zoho Sign or another electronic signature platform. Each counterpart is deemed an original, and all counterparts together form one instrument.
draft.notes: Replaces the current "prepare and sign 2 copies" wet-ink language, which does not match confirmed actual signing practice.

must_have.required_content: Named signatories with position and email, matching however many people actually sign each side.
must_have.rationale: A mismatched block creates a later question about whether the signed version is authentic.

draft.language:
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

For and on behalf of Start2:
Name: _____ Position: _____ Email: _____ Signature: _____
Name: _____ Position: _____ Email: _____ Signature: _____

For and on behalf of Company:
Name: _____ Position: _____ Email: _____ Signature: _____
Name: _____ Position: _____ Email: _____ Signature: _____
draft.notes: Standardised to two lines each side across all five country templates.

good_to_have.description: Either party may terminate without cause on a stated notice period.
good_to_have.negotiation_stance: Push for it, mutual only. Pay for work done to date, plus retain any non-refundable tranche already paid. Drop if resisted, most Start2 programs are short enough that the exposure is limited.

draft.language: Either Party may terminate this Agreement without cause on [X] days' written notice. On such termination, Start2 is entitled to payment for work performed to date and to retain any non-refundable amount already paid.
draft.notes: Notice period open. Push for this mutually, drop if resisted, most programs are short enough that the exposure is limited.

good_to_have.clause: Non-solicitation of Start2 network. Runs client-to-Start2 only, not the reverse: Start2 is the one exposing its network, the client is not exposing an equivalent network in most engagement types.
good_to_have.description: No solicitation of Start2's mentors, experts and program staff for a defined period after the program ends.
good_to_have.negotiation_stance: Push for it, especially in delegation and matching programs where the client gets direct access to Start2's network.

draft.language: For [X] months after this Agreement ends, Company shall not solicit or engage any mentor, expert, or program staff member introduced to it by Start2 in connection with the Service, without Start2's prior written consent.

good_to_have.description: Each party confirms it has not made or received improper payments in connection with the agreement.
good_to_have.negotiation_stance: Push for it, especially with government-linked or state-owned clients.

draft.language: Each Party warrants that it has not made or received, and shall not make or receive, any improper payment or benefit in connection with this Agreement, and shall comply with applicable anti-bribery and corruption law.

nice_to_have.description: Permission to name the client as a reference client after the program.
A named operational contact on each side, separate from the signatory.
If one clause is found unenforceable, the rest of the agreement stands.

nice_to_have_rule: Rule for all items on this sheet: ask once. Drop immediately if resisted.

G1.language: Either Party may terminate this Agreement without cause on [X] days' written notice. On such termination, Start2 is entitled to payment for work performed to date and to retain any non-refundable amount already paid.
G1.notes: Notice period open. Push for this mutually, drop if resisted, most programs are short enough that the exposure is limited.

G2.language: For [X] months after this Agreement ends, Company shall not solicit or engage any mentor, expert, or program staff member introduced to it by Start2 in connection with the Service, without Start2's prior written consent.

G3.language: Each Party warrants that it has not made or received, and shall not make or receive, any improper payment or benefit in connection with this Agreement, and shall comply with applicable anti-bribery and corruption law.

N1.language: Start2 may name Company as a reference client in its marketing materials after the Service concludes, unless Company objects in writing.

N2.language: Each Party shall name an operational contact for day-to-day matters under this Agreement, separate from the signatory named in Clause [Notices].

N3.language: If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force, and the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the unenforceable provision with one of similar commercial effect.

decisions.options:
(a) Keep 50/50 default
(b) Move to 100% upfront as default
(c) Staged upfront tied to program phases
decisions.recommendation_claude: a) 50/50 default - 50% upon signing of contract and 50% upon completion of service. Completion of Service is to be defined.
decisions.recommendation_usa: a) 50/50 default - 50% upon signing of contract and 50% upon completion of service. Completion of Service is to be defined.
decisions.affects: Cash exposure. Fee, currency, and payment clause (draft clause 5) in all five templates.

decisions.decision: Liability cap multiple for confidentiality/data/IP breaches
decisions.options:
(a) Same cap as general liability (total fees)
(b) A stated multiple of total fees (2x, 3x)
decisions.recommendation_claude: (b), 2x total fees as a starting ask. These breach types carry third-party exposure the general cap was not built for.
decisions.affects: Caps sheet. Limitation of liability clause (draft clause 17).

decisions.recommendation_claude: 3 business days if using the unmodified Start2 template. 5 business days if clauses are updated from the template or the client's own template is used.
decisions.recommendation_usa: 3 business days if using the unmodified Start2 template. 5 business days if clauses are updated from the template or the client's own template is used.
decisions.affects: Process & Authority sheet. Sales team expectations.

decisions.recommendation_claude: Every contract, regardless of fee, template or inserted clauses, is sent for sign-off before signature, in this order: 1. Director of People and Operations; 2. Regional Director of Innovation and Product Strategy; 3. CEO.
decisions.recommendation_usa: Every contract, regardless of fee, template or inserted clauses, is sent for sign-off before signature, in this order: 1. Director of People and Operations; 2. Regional Director of Innovation and Product Strategy; 3. CEO.

decisions.decision: Approval required by CEO (superseded by D-04)
decisions.recommendation_claude: Superseded by D-04: CEO is the third and final approver on every contract.
decisions.recommendation_usa: Superseded by D-04: CEO is the third and final approver on every contract.

decisions.decision: Long-stop period for prolonged force majeure termination
decisions.options:
(a) 30 days
(b) 60 days
(c) Tie it to a fraction of the remaining term (e.g. force majeure exceeding half the remaining term)
decisions.recommendation_claude: (b), 60 days as a default. Long enough that ordinary short disruptions don't trigger an exit right either side didn't want, short enough that a program stuck for two months has a way out.
decisions.affects: Must Have: Force majeure (draft clauses 18.2 and 18.3). Force Majeure clause across all five templates.

decisions.decision: Fee treatment on force majeure cancellation: recover costs only, or retain the whole fee
decisions.options:
(a) Start2 recovers only costs actually committed or paid to third parties (current Must Have: Cost recovery on cancellation approach)
(b) Start2 retains the entire Service Fee already paid, credited toward a future or rescheduled program, regardless of costs actually incurred
decisions.recommendation_claude: (a) Start2 recovers only costs actually committed or paid to third parties (current Must Have: Cost recovery on cancellation approach)
decisions.recommendation_usa: (a) Start2 recovers only costs actually committed or paid to third parties (current Must Have: Cost recovery on cancellation approach)
decisions.affects: Must Have: Cost recovery on cancellation. Interacts with D-01 (payment terms).

client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable only if narrowly scoped to a named list of direct competitors, for the term only, no post-term tail.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject if scope is "any competitor" undefined, or extends beyond the term.

client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Start2 delivers a defined service, not a guaranteed outcome. Acceptable fallback: a service-credit remedy for a defined, Start2-caused failure to deliver a specific deliverable.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject any clawback tied to outcomes Start2 does not control (deals closed, funding raised, startups placed).

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Unlimited liability, or liability tied to client's total spend across all engagements
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Counter with the fee-based cap in the Caps sheet.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Hard stop. Escalate before conceding any movement here.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Assignment of IP created during the program to the client
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable: client owns work product specific to their own startups' outputs.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject if it extends to Start2's methodology, curriculum, or any tool built for general use across clients.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Governing law switched to client's jurisdiction (non-contracting-entity home)
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable fallback: neutral third-jurisdiction arbitration (e.g. SIAC) before conceding client's home courts.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject litigation (not arbitration) in the client's home jurisdiction outright for government-adjacent clients where enforcement against Start2 assets there is a real prospect.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Payment terms beyond 30 days, or tied to client's own downstream funding
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Start2's cash position does not carry client-side financing risk.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject. See no-cost-before-payment rule in Process & Authority.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Confidentiality carve-out for disclosure to client's parent/affiliates without consent
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable only if "affiliates" is defined (majority-owned entities only) and bound by the same confidentiality terms in writing before disclosure.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject an undefined or unbounded affiliate carve-out.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Insurance requirement (minimum cover, evidence, or additional-insured status)
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable, provided the coverage amount is proportionate to the deal size rather than an arbitrary institutional minimum, and limited to providing a certificate of insurance on request, not open-ended audit rights.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject if the required cover is disproportionate to the contract value, or if the client demands ongoing audit rights beyond a certificate, or insists on being named as an additional insured on the policy itself.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Audit rights (client or government auditor access to Start2's records)
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable, limited to records and documentation directly relating to Service delivery and fee calculation under this specific Agreement, requested within a defined period after the Service ends (12 months), with at least 15 business days' prior written notice, no more than once in that period, and only where the auditor is bound by confidentiality at least as strict as Clause [Confidentiality]. Start2 may charge a reasonable fee to cover the cost of facilitating the inspection.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject if the right has no time limit, extends to Start2's general financial records or other clients' engagements, reaches Start2's own IP or methodology beyond what's needed to confirm delivery, allows unannounced or unlimited-frequency access, is not subject to auditor confidentiality, or the client refuses to pay a reasonable facilitation fee.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Payment suspension or clawback based on an alleged misstatement
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable only if triggered by a finding, not a bare allegation, following written notice and a reasonable opportunity for Start2 to respond before any suspension or clawback takes effect.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject a right to suspend payment or claw back amounts already paid based solely on an unproven allegation, with no defined process, notice, or opportunity to respond.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Revenue contingent on a minimum threshold (e.g. minimum confirmed participants or bookings)
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable only if Start2 recovers costs already committed under the Cost Recovery on Cancellation clause if the minimum threshold is not met, since real preparatory work and third-party costs are often committed before the threshold is confirmed.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject a structure with zero fee and zero cost recovery if the minimum threshold fails, particularly where Start2 has already performed preparatory work at the client's request.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: EU or government grant flow-down audit rights (e.g. OLAF, European Court of Auditors)
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Generally non-negotiable where the client is itself bound by EU or government grant funding rules, this flows down from the client's own funding obligations rather than being the client's choice. Accept as a standing exception distinct from the general Audit rights clause, but flag internally whenever it appears, since it exceeds Start2's normal negotiated audit position: no time limit, no notice period, no fee, no confidentiality protection for the auditor, and it reaches third-party institutions beyond the contracting party.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: There isn't a real rejection threshold in the usual sense, refusing it likely means being unable to contract with EU-grant-funded clients at all. Escalate when this appears.

client_inserted_clauses.clause: Liquidated damages or a fixed penalty per breach
client_inserted_clauses.start2_position: Acceptable only if the penalty is capped in aggregate across all breaches and is credited against, not stacked on top of, the overall liability cap.
client_inserted_clauses.rejection_threshold: Reject an uncapped per-offense penalty with no aggregate ceiling, repeated technical breaches could otherwise produce a penalty disproportionate to the total contract value.

caps.item: Direct loss under limitation of liability
caps.measure: Total Service Fee paid or payable under the agreement
caps.notes: Already the effect of the current indemnity clause. Needs to be visible as its own clause (see Must Have: Limitation of liability).

caps.measure: Defined multiple of the Service Fee (figure is yours to set, see Decision D-02)
caps.notes: Should carry a higher cap than the general liability cap.

caps.measure: Same higher, defined multiple, not the general cap
caps.notes: Client is exposed to real third-party claims if Start2's materials infringe someone else's IP.
Already carved out of the cap in the current indemnity clause. Correct, keep uncapped.
Should be added and kept uncapped.

caps.item: Confidentiality duty itself (not the damages cap)
caps.drafted_in: Confidentiality's own clause 8.4, and Survival, which lists Clause [Confidentiality] among the surviving clauses

execution_checks.check: Every bracketed placeholder ([XXX], COMPANY DESCRIPTION, [Insert commencement event]) is filled. A signed agreement with a placeholder still in it is a live incident, not a defect, escalate immediately.
Clause numbering is sequential and matches any cross-references elsewhere in the document.
Term dates in the recitals, the term clause, and Annex/Appendix all agree with each other.
Contracting entity name is identical everywhere it appears: cover page, signature block, bank details, and any Chinese or Korean-language mirror text.
Bilingual agreements: the two language versions say the same thing on fee, term dates, and liability cap at minimum. Have a fluent reviewer confirm, do not assume.
Signature block has the right number of lines for the actual signing parties, no blank line left for a party who will not sign.
Bank details in the payment clause match the named contracting entity, not a different Start2 entity.
No leftover tracked-change or redline artifacts in the body text.
Appendix or Schedule numbers referenced in the body match what is actually attached, no reference to a Schedule that doesn't exist.
Appendix content is specific to this deal, not another client's scope carried over from a previous draft.
Every bracketed clause cross-reference (e.g. "Clause [Cost Recovery on Cancellation]") has been replaced with the actual clause number before signature, none left as literal brackets.
Currency, fee figures, governing law, and arbitration body match the actual contracting entity for this deal, not copy-paste residue from a different country's last draft.

passes.what_to_check: Fee, currency, payment trigger, term dates. Unique to every deal and most likely to contain a blank or an error. Check before spending time on boilerplate that rarely changes.
Anything not in the base template. Deal-specific risk concentrates here. Run each one against the Client-Inserted Clauses sheet.
Compare the draft against the current clean template clause by clause. Flag any altered standard clause even if it looks harmless.
Run the Execution Check sheet as a final pass once content is settled, since formatting and cross-reference errors are often introduced during earlier edit rounds.

process_and_authority.rule: Signing, initialling, portal click-through acceptance, email confirmation of terms, and verbal agreement to terms. A portal click-through or an email saying "we agree to the attached" is a signature for these purposes.
Recommended minimum 3 business days between a complete draft reaching the reviewer and the earliest possible signature date, for a deal using the unmodified base template.

process_and_authority.topic: Lead time, deal with client-inserted clause
process_and_authority.rule: Recommended minimum 5 business days, to allow checking the client clause against a rejection threshold, sometimes needing a second opinion.

Every contract, regardless of fee, template or inserted clauses, is sent for sign-off before signature, in this order: 1. Director of People and Operations; 2. Regional Director of Innovation and Product Strategy; 3. CEO. Nothing is signed, initialled, or accepted before all three have approved.

process_and_authority.topic: Client says the contract cannot be changed: first response
process_and_authority.rule: Ask what specifically cannot move: term sheet or actual signed document. "Cannot be changed" often means "cannot be changed after our internal sign-off," which a side letter solves without reopening their master document.
Use when the client's own paper is the vehicle (they issued the contract) and only one or two terms need to move. Amends specific numbered clauses of their document without touching their template.
Use when Start2's own template is the vehicle and the client wants something added rather than changed.
For public tenders, clarification questions submitted before bid submission become part of the contract once awarded. This is the point of maximum leverage, before the bid is submitted.

process_and_authority.topic: Point after which leverage is gone
process_and_authority.rule: Once the client has announced the partnership publicly, committed program dates to their own stakeholders, or (public sector) the tender is awarded. A firm line on a Critical item is still worth holding past this point. A firm line on a Good-to-have item is not, drop it.

process_and_authority.topic: No external cost before payment received
process_and_authority.rule: No mentor fee, venue booking, travel booking, or subcontractor engagement is committed against a client deal until the payment tranche that funds it has actually landed in Start2's account. Not invoiced. Landed.
